Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation.

84 * 42 * 7 * 5 * 21 * 93
questions.solution:
BODMAS Rule:

Given equation: 84 * 42 * 7 * 5 * 21 * 93

Option 1) +, ÷, −, ×, =

After put the mathematical sing we get:

⇒ 84 + 42 ÷ 7 - 5 × 21 = 93

⇒ 84 + 6 - 5 × 21 = 93

⇒ 84 + 6 - 105 = 93

⇒ 90 - 105 = 93

⇒ - 15 ≠ 93

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) ×, ÷, +, −, =

After put the mathematical sing we get:

⇒ 84 × 42 ÷ 7 + 5 - 21 = 93

⇒ 84 × 6 + 5 - 21 = 93

⇒ 504 + 5 - 21 = 93

⇒ 509 - 21 = 93

⇒ 488 ≠ 93

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) +, ÷, ×, −, =

After put the mathematical sing we get:

⇒ 84 + 42 ÷ 7 × 5 - 21 = 93 

⇒ 84 + 6 × 5 - 21 = 93

⇒ 84 + 30 - 21 = 93

⇒ 114 - 21 = 93

⇒ 93 = 93

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 4) ÷, +, ×, −, =

After put the mathematical sing we get:

⇒ 84 ÷ 42 + 7 × 5 - 21 = 93 

⇒ 2 + 7 × 5 - 21 = 93

⇒ 2 + 30 - 21 = 93

⇒ 32 - 21 = 93

⇒ 11 ≠ 93

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "+, ÷, ×, −, =".

questions.questionHtml: If the numbers ‘18’ and ‘30’ are interchanged, then which of the following equations can be correctly balanced?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Rule:

If the numbers ‘18’ and ‘30’ are interchanged,

Let check all options one by one.

Option 1) 12 – 30 × 18 ÷ 3 + 16 = 174

After interchanging the digit we get:

⇒ 12 – 18 × 30 ÷ 3 + 16 = 174

⇒ 12 - 18 × 10 + 16 = 174

⇒ 12 - 180 + 16 = 174

⇒ 28 - 180 = 174

⇒ - 152 ≠ 174

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) 14 × 5 – 18 ÷ 6 + 30 = 73

After interchanging the digit we get:

⇒ 14 × 5 – 30 ÷ 6 + 18 = 73

⇒ 14 × 5 - 5 + 18 = 73

⇒ 70 - 5 + 18 = 73

⇒ 88 - 5 = 73

⇒ 83 ≠ 73

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) 35 ÷ 5 × 5 + 30 – 18 = 23

After interchanging the digit we get:

⇒ 35 ÷ 5 × 5 + 18 – 30 = 23

⇒ 7 × 5 + 18 - 30 = 23

⇒ 35 + 18 - 30 = 23

⇒ 53 - 30 = 23

⇒ 23 = 23

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 4) 64 + 18 × 5 ÷ 3 – 30 = 98

After interchanging the digit we get:

⇒ 64 + 30 × 5 ÷ 3 – 18 = 98

⇒ 64 + 30 × 1.666 - 18 = 98

⇒ 64 + 49.98 - 18 = 98

⇒ 113.98 - 18 = 98

⇒ 95.98 ≠ 98

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "35 ÷ 5 × 5 + 30 – 18 = 23".

questions.question: The ______ lies above the mesopause and is a region in which temperatures increase with height.
questions.questionHtml: The ______ lies above the mesopause and is a region in which temperatures increase with height.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is thermosphere.

Key Points

  • The thermosphere lies above the mesopause and is a region in which temperatures increase with height.
  • Thermosphere:
    • In the thermosphere, the temperature rises very rapidly with increasing height.
    • The ionosphere is a part of this layer.
    • It extends between 80-400 km. This layer helps in radio transmission.

Additional Information

  • There are a total of five atmospheric layers. These are -
    • Troposphere.
    • Stratosphere.
    • Mesosphere.
    • Thermosphere.
    • Ionosphere: the lowest part of the Thermosphere contains the ionosphere.
    • Exosphere.
  • Stratosphere:
    • It lies beyond the troposphere, up to an altitude of 50 km from the earth's surface.
    • The temperature in this layer remains constant for some distance but then rises to reach a level of 0°C at 50 km altitude.
    • This rise is due to the presence of ozone.
    • This layer is almost free from clouds and associated weather phenomena, making conditions most ideal for flying aeroplanes.
  • Exosphere:
    • This is the uppermost layer of the atmosphere extending beyond the ionosphere above a height of about 400 km.
    • The air is extremely rarefied and the temperature gradually increases through the layer.
    • Light gases like helium and hydrogen float into space from here.
  • Troposphere:
    • It is the lowermost layer of the atmosphere.
    • The layer starts at Earth's surface and extends 8 to 14.5 km high (5 to 9 miles).
    • The troposphere contains dust particles and water vapour.
    • This is the most important layer of the atmosphere because all kinds of weather changes take place only in this layer.
    • The zone dividing troposphere from the stratosphere is known as the tropopause.

questions.question: Which of the following is the LEAST visible form of land erosion?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the LEAST visible form of land erosion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sheet erosion.

Key Points

  • Sheet erosion is the LEAST visible form of land erosion.
  • Sheet erosion is the process of uniform removal of soil in thin layers by the forces of raindrops on land.
  • It is caused by the force of rainfall.
  • It takes place in levelled lands and plowed fields after a heavy shower and the soil, removal is not easily noticeable, but it is harmful since it removes the finer and more fertile topsoil.

Additional Information

  • Rill and gully erosion:
    • In rill erosion, finger-like rills appear on the cultivated land after it has undergone sheet erosion.
    • These rills are usually smoothened out every year while forming.
    • Each year the rills slowly increase in number and become wider and deeper.
    • Gully erosion is the removal of soil along drainage lines by surface water runoff.
    • When rills increase in size, they become gullies.
    • Once started, gullies will continue to move by headward erosion or by slumping of the side walls.
    • Gullies formed over a large area give rise to badland topography (Chambal Ravines).
    • When a gully bed is eroded further due to headward erosion, the bed gradually deepens and flattens out, and a ravine is formed.
    • The depth of a ravine may extend to 30 meters.
  • Landslides
    • Landslides and slope instability cause problems in many parts of the world.
    • A landslide is primarily a combination of several geological processes that include physical factors like earth movements like extensive slope failure, rocks falling, and debris flow.
    • These ground movements may take place in a coastal, offshore, or far onshore environment.
    • Gravity, in addition to other factors that affect ground stability, is the main force that causes landslides.
    • Normally, the ground characteristics develop particular sub-surface soil conditions that cause slope failure.
    • However, the real landslide needs a trigger before it can be initiated. It is normally feasible to recognize the main landslide origin and the landslide triggers.

  • Symptoms include loss of consciousness, sudden twitching, etc.

  • It is considered one of the most common neurological diseases globally.
  • Nearly 80% of people with epilepsy live in low- and middle-income countries.

Key Points

  • He was the court physician of Kaniska.
  • Charaka was one of the principal contributors to Ayurveda medicine in ancient India.
  • He is best known for his work Charaka Samhita.
  • Charaka Samhita:
    • It is also called Caraka-Samhita.
    • It is a detailed text on ancient Indian medicine attributed to Charaka, a practitioner of Ayurveda, India's traditional medical system.
    • Charaka-Samhita, also spelt Caraka-Samhita or Caraka- samhita, comprehensive text on ancient Indian medicine credited to Charaka.
    • He was a practitioner of the traditional system of Indian medicine known as Ayurveda.
    • Charaka is thought to have flourished sometime between the 2nd century BCE and the 2nd century CE.

    • The Agnivesha-Samhita, written by Agnivesha, was unlike any other in terms of depth and quality.

questions.question: A reduction of 20% in the price of bananas enables a customer to buy 6 more bananas for ₹80. What is the reduced price of bananas per dozen (in ₹)?
questions.questionHtml: A reduction of 20% in the price of bananas enables a customer to buy 6 more bananas for ₹80. What is the reduced price of bananas per dozen (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
Let the original price of a banana be 5x, new price will be 4x(reduced by 20%)

⇒ \(80\over 4x\) - \(80\over 5x\) = 6 ⇒ \({80 (5 - 4)}\over 4 \times 5 \times x\) = 6 ⇒ \({80 (5 - 4)}\over 20 \times x\) = 6

⇒ \(4\over x\) = 6 ⇒ x = \(2\over3\)

The new price of bananas is ⇒ 4x = 4 ×\(2\over3\)

The price per dozen is ⇒ 4 × \(2\over3\) × 12 = 32

questions.question: The total surface area of a right pyramid, with base as a square of side 8 cm, is 208 cm 2 . What is the slant height (in cm) of the pyramid?

questions.solution:
Given:

Total surface area of a right pyramid, with base as a square of side 8 cm, is 208 cm2

Formula used:

Total surface area = Lateral surface area + Area of the base

Lateral surface area = 1/2 × Perimeter of base × slant height

Calculation:

According to the question,

208 = Lateral surface area + 82

⇒ 208 - 64 = Lateral surface area

⇒ 144 = Lateral surface area

Again,

144 = 1/2 × 4 × 8 × slant height

⇒ 144/16 = slant height

⇒ 9 = slant height

∴ The slant height (in cm) of the pyramid is 9.

Given:

Concept used:

If the sum of digits of the number is divisible by 9, then the number itself is divisible by 9.

If the difference of the sum of alternative digits of a number is divisible by 11 or 0, then that number is divisible by 11 completely.

Calculation:

99 = 9 × 11

So, the number should be divisible by both 9 and 11

Now,

4 + 8 + k + 2 + 0 + 4 + 8 + p + 6 = 32 + k + p

Now,

Possible values of k + p = 4, 13

Again,

(4 + k + 0 + 8 + 6) - (8 + 2 + 4 + p) = 0 or multiple of 11

⇒ 18 + k - 14 - p = 0 or multiple of 11

⇒ 4 + k - p = 0 or multiple of 11

Now, 

k - p can be - 4 or 7

Now,

For k + p = 4 and k - p = - 4

We can say by adding both 2k = 0

⇒ k = 0

So, p = 4   [Both are possible]

Again,

For k + p = 4 and k - p = 7

We can say by adding both 2k = 11

⇒ k = 5.5  [Not possible]

Again,

For k + p = 13 and k - p = - 4

We can say by adding both 2k = 9

⇒ k = 4.5  [Not possible]

Again,

For k + p = 13 and k - p = 7

We can say by adding both 2k = 20

⇒ k = 10  [Not possible]

So, only possible values of k and p is 0 and 4

Now,

k × p = 0 × 4

⇒ 0

∴ Required answer is 0.

questions.question: If \(6{\sqrt6}\) p 3 + \(2\sqrt2\) q 3 = ( \(\sqrt6\) p + \(\sqrt2\) q)(Sp 2 + Mq 2 - Npq), then the positive value of \(\sqrt{S^2+M^2+2N^2}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(6{\sqrt6}\) p3 + \(2\sqrt2\) q3 = (\(\sqrt6\) p + \(\sqrt2\) q)(Sp2 + Mq2 - Npq), then the positive value of \(\sqrt{S^2+M^2+2N^2}\) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(6{\sqrt6}\) p3 + \(2\sqrt2\) q3 = (\(\sqrt6\) p + \(\sqrt2\) q)(Sp2 + Mq2 - Npq)

Concept used:

a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 + b2 - ab)

Calculation:

\(6{\sqrt6}\) p3 + \(2\sqrt2\) q3 = (\(\sqrt6\) p + \(\sqrt2\) q)[(\(\sqrt6\)p)2 + (\(\sqrt2\)q)2 - \(\sqrt6\) × \(\sqrt2\)pq)

⇒ (\(\sqrt6\) p + \(\sqrt2\) q)(6p2 + 2q2 - \(\sqrt{12}\)pq)

So,

S = 6

M = 2

N = \(\sqrt{12}\)

Now,

\(\sqrt{S^2+M^2+2N^2}\) = \(\sqrt{6^2+2^2+2 \times\sqrt{12}^2}\)

⇒ \(\sqrt{36+4+2 \times12}\)

⇒ \(\sqrt{36+4+24}\)

⇒ \(\sqrt{40+24}\)

⇒ \(\sqrt{64}\)

⇒ 8

∴ Required answer is 8.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, X and Y are the points on sides AB and AC, respectively, such that XY is parallel to BC. If XY : BC = 2.5 : 7, what is the ratio of the area of the trapezium BCYX to that of the ΔAXY?
questions.questionHtml: In triangle ABC, X and Y are the points on sides AB and AC, respectively, such that  XY is parallel to BC. If XY : BC = 2.5 : 7, what is the ratio of the area of the trapezium BCYX to that of the ΔAXY?
questions.solution:
Given:

In a ΔABC, X and Y on AB and AC respectively

XY ∥ BC

XY : BC = 2.5 : 7 

Formula used:

In two similar triangles, the ratio of the area is equal to the ratio of the square of their corresponding sides.

Calculation:

Here,

XY : BC = 2.5 : 7 

As, It is given that XY || BC

So, ΔAXY ~ ΔABC

(Area of ΔAXY)/(Area of ΔABC) = (XY/BC)2

⇒ (Area of ΔAXY)/(Area of ΔABC) = (2.5/7)2

⇒ (Area of ΔAXY)/(Area of ΔABC) = 6.25/49

Now,

Area of ΔAXY = 6.25

So, area of trapezium BCYX = 49 - 6.25

⇒ 42.75

Ratio = 42.75/6.25

⇒ 171/25

∴ The ratio of the area of the trapezium BCYX to that of the ΔAXY is \(171\over25\).

questions.question: AB is a chord in the minor segment of a circle with center O. C is a point between A and B on the minor arc AB. The tangents to the circle at A and B meet at the point D. If ∠ACB = 116°, then the measure of ∠ADB is
questions.questionHtml: AB is a chord in the minor segment of a circle with center O. C is a point between A and B on the minor arc AB. The tangents to the circle at A and B meet at the point D. If ∠ACB = 116°, then the measure of ∠ADB is
questions.solution:
Given:

∠ACB = 116°

Concept Used:

When a quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle, the opposite angles of it are supplementary angles.

The angle subtended at the center is always double the angle subtended at the remaining arc.

The radius from the center of the circle to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

Calculation:

Point P is taken on the major arc of the circle.

Then, A & P, B & P, C & B, and A & C are joined.

From cyclic quadrilateral APBC

∠ACB = 116°

Now, ∠APB = (180 – 116)° = 64°

Now, ∠AOB = (64 × 2)°

⇒ 128°

Since OA = OB = radius of the circle

So, from quadrilateral AOBD

∠ADB = 360° - (∠OBD + ∠OAD + ∠AOB)

⇒ ∠ADB = 360° - (90° + 90° + 128°)

⇒ ∠ADB = 360° - 308°

⇒ ⇒ ∠ADB = 52° 

∴ The required measure of ∠ADB is 52°.
